## Why This Is Asked

- Atomic operations and memory_order semantics

## Code Example

```javascript
// Pseudo-C: fair ticket lock (conceptual, not compilable)
typedef struct { _Atomic uint32_t next; _Atomic uint32_t owner; } tt_lock;
void tt_lock(tt_lock* l){ uint32_t my=atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&l->next,1,memory_order_relaxed); while(atomic_load_explicit(&l->owner,memory_order_acquire)!=my); thread_local_uint32 = my; }
void tt_unlock(tt_lock* l){ uint32_t my=thread_local_uint32; atomic_store_explicit(&l->owner,my+1,memory_order_release); }
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates the ability to design crash-safe concurrent data structures for non-volatile memory, assessing understanding of flush semantics, recovery mechanisms, and performance tradeoffs under contention.

## Key Concepts
- Persistent memory programming model and hardware semantics
- Write-ahead logging and flush primitives (CLWB, SFENCE)
- Per-slot version counters to prevent ABA problems
- Recovery procedures and WAL replay
- Memory ordering and cache-line alignment for performance

## Design Choice: Open Addressing
Linear probing with open addressing is preferred for NVRAM due to superior cache-line alignment, which minimizes unnecessary writes to persistent media, simplified recovery logic without traversing linked structures, and the elimination of pointer overhead inherent in chaining implementations.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical memory allocator design under NUMA pressure, focusing on stability, ABA avoidance, and performance with real-time burst workloads.

## Key Concepts
- NUMA locality and per-node memory pools
- Slab/arena allocation strategies
- Hazard pointers for safe memory reclamation
- Cache-line alignment and padding to avoid false sharing
- Cross-socket refill mechanisms and work-stealing

## Code Example
```c
// Skeleton API: slab_alloc, slab_free
typedef struct slab { /* block metadata */ } slab_t;
void* slab_alloc(size_t sz); // 4KB blocks
void slab_free(void* ptr);
```

## Microbenchmark Design
The benchmark would simulate bursty allocations across sockets with threads performing rapid alloc/free cycles, measuring throughput under NUMA-local vs cross-socket memory access patterns.
